description: A vector terrain behind the Start page, after Battlezone and the vector arcade games (#607): wireframe mountains on a horizon below the Omnibar, a perspective grid on the ground before them and a wireframe crescent moon low in the sky, in thin palette-coloured lines with a vector monitor's glow. The browser draws it (src/ui/VectorTerrain.qml); the website does not. Lengths are shares of the scene's width or height unless named otherwise; times are in seconds. A colour is a role (ground, light, glow, skyTop, skyLow, groundNear, black, white) or a mix of two at an amount. `pitch` is 2 rather than the other Scenes' 4, so a line is thin, and `crt` is the road's glass at the road's size on screen: its pixel counts are doubled. `rest` is where the Omnibar rests, as a share of the height. `peaks`: the highest peak stands `gap` CSS pixels below the resting Omnibar's hint row, which the browser hands in and which reaches `omnibarReach` below where the Omnibar rests at the theme's type size, and the ground's horizon lies `share` of the way from there to the bottom edge, so the mountains, as tall as that space at most, stay below the Omnibar. `lines` are `width` of the Scene's pixels wide, each with a glow `blur` of its pixels around it at `alpha` of its colour; in a Private window a line is the light mixed toward the ground by `unlit`, with no glow. `ridges` are the mountains, far to near, each a range of `peaks` peaks on a loop the scene's width long: a peak stands `height` [from, span] of the mountains' space high where `seed` scatters it, a valley `valley` of the space at most, and a facet line falls from each peak to the ground `facet` of the way to the next valley. At rest a range drifts sideways `drift` of the width a second; nearer ranges drift faster. Its fill is the ground, so a nearer range hides a farther one and the moon. `still` is how far, in seconds of drift, a still or Private terrain has drifted. `omnibar` is where the resting Omnibar's field stands, which the moon keeps clear: its top edge `above` CSS pixels above where it rests, `widest` CSS pixels wide at most and `margin` in from either side. `moon` is a wireframe crescent, its radius `radius` of the width or the height, whichever is less, low in the sky beside the Omnibar: `across` the width, or further out to clear the Omnibar by `gap`, its centre `lift` radii above the highest peak. Where the page area has no room beside the Omnibar, it stands `across` the width, as far in as it must to stay on the page, `gap` above the Omnibar's top edge; a circle as large cuts it, its centre `phase` radii from the moon's toward its dark side, which faces `tilt` degrees clockwise from the right. `grid` is the ground: `radials` lines each side of the middle, `spread` of the half width apart at the bottom edge, running from depth `far` toward the reader; and `count` lines across, `spacing` apart in depth, each fading in over `fadeFar` from the far end and out over the last `fadeNear` before the bottom edge. At rest the grid holds still; from a commit until the page paints its lines rush toward the reader at `rush` depth units a second, the speed easing toward that at `ease` and back down after the page has painted, over a frame of at most `longestStep`. `still` is where a still or Private grid stands, in depth units.
name: Vector terrain
